comment: Controlled facet vocabularies for resource.yaml (CONTRACT.md §5). resource.schema.json points facets.domains and facets.modalities at these lists ($ref domains.json#/domains, domains.json#/modalities), and validate-library rejects any token not listed here. Grown only by PR to this file: add the token, keep the list sorted, and add a one-line entry in notes when the meaning is not obvious from the name. lifecycle (build|launch|grow|support) stays inline in resource.schema.json — it is a fixed four-stage enum (CONTRACT.md §2), not a growing vocabulary.

notes._domains: Topical areas a resource belongs to; every skill, tool, example, and reference carries at least two. Derived from the 2026-09-02 resource.yaml audit (59 tokens in use) plus editor, added 2026-09-03 for editor-session tools that had no honest second domain.
notes._modalities: What a resource produces or touches (scenes, scripts, shaders, assets, images, audio, video, docs, ...). Enumerated because the 12 values in use were already consistent.
notes.agent-workflow: How an agent should work — process skills such as brainstorming, planning, verification — not a game topic.
notes.asset-import: Templates or tools centered on importing external asset kits.
notes.builtin: Templates generated in-process by summer create, with no satellite-repo pin.
notes.creator: Summercraft creator API — publishing .pck builds, releases, shared config.
notes.editor: Tools that inspect or mutate the open editor session: scene-tree nodes, selection, inspector, Output panel, open and save scene tabs.
notes.file: Raw project-file access (read, write, replace text) rather than scene- or node-level operations.
notes.generate: Summer Studio generation — image, 3D, audio, video, motion — and the job plumbing around it.
notes.headless: Running the engine without the editor UI (shell, CI).
notes.meta: Resources about Summer itself — skills about skills, library feedback, the CLI/MCP surface.
notes.playtest: Driving and observing the running game as a tester — deterministic launches, frame stepping, synthetic or recorded input, frame-stamped probes. Distinct from runtime (the running game as a target) and verification (proving work landed).
notes.runtime: The running game as opposed to the editor scene: play/stop, runtime tree, debugger output.
notes.verification: Checking that work actually landed — screenshots, snapshots, probes, run-and-inspect.
